author: reek
body: The file manager -- H4e's first app on the desktop. It browses the boot medium's ESP through the same GopFat16 mount every storage screen uses, riding the medium lock, so the volume on the glass is the volume the machine booted from. The list is the directory's decoded entries; Enter or a click descends into a directory or opens a byte view of a file; Esc climbs back up and finally returns to the desktop.

author: reek
body: The row under a screen point, or -1: shared by hover and click so the two can never disagree about what the pointer is on.

author: reek
body: Keep the selection on screen: the top row follows the selection when it walks off either edge of the window.

author: reek
body: One preview line: n bytes as hex then the same n as printable ASCII, the shape every hex viewer trains an eye for.

author: reek
body: A Codex source file gets its source drawn and coloured; everything else gets the hex dump. The stick carries its own source as SOURCE.SRC, so this is the screen on which a person reads the machine's own text on the machine, and reading it as sixteen bytes of hex per line was a poor way to do that.

author: reek
body: The test is the 8.3 EXTENSION and not the name, because FAT16 has no other place to put the answer: a `.codex` file cannot survive 8.3 with its extension intact, and the extension is the only field a directory entry has that says what kind of thing this is.

author: reek
body: A line ends at byte 10, or at the end of what was read. The preview holds one sector, so the last line is usually cut mid-way; that is honest for a preview and the classifier is written to tolerate it, including a string left unterminated by the cut.

author: reek
body: One drawn line per source line, and one `gop-draw-text` per RUN rather than per character: a run is already a contiguous span of one colour, which is exactly what the text primitive draws, so the colouring costs no more calls than the number of tokens on the line.

author: reek
body: The descent is two parallel stacks -- the cluster of every directory on the path (a negative sentinel names the FAT16 fixed root) and its name for the title bar. Pop rebuilds all but the last; the lists are a screen deep at most.

author: reek
body: One sector answers the whole view. An empty file has no cluster to read and says so honestly.

author: reek
body: The cursor hides BEFORE a repaint and is re-placed after: the pane covers only part of the panel, so clearing the flag without restoring would leave the old cursor pixels standing on the sidebar and bake them into the next saved patch.

author: reek
body: Mounting rides the medium lock; a machine with no readable ESP gets an honest pane and a way back.
